From bb0a2675f72b458e64f47071e8aabdb225a6af4d Mon Sep 17 00:00:00 2001
From: =?UTF-8?q?Martin=20Hundeb=C3=B8ll?= <mnhu@prevas.dk>
Date: Wed, 19 Jul 2017 08:17:02 +0200
Subject: [PATCH] net: dsa: mv88e6xxx: Enable CMODE config support for 6390X
MIME-Version: 1.0
Content-Type: text/plain; charset=UTF-8
Content-Transfer-Encoding: 8bit

Commit f39908d3b1c45 ('net: dsa: mv88e6xxx: Set the CMODE for mv88e6390
ports 9 & 10') added support for setting the CMODE for the 6390X family,
but only enabled it for 9290 and 6390 - and left out 6390X.

Fix support for setting the CMODE on 6390X also by assigning
mv88e6390x_port_set_cmode() to the .port_set_cmode function pointer in
mv88e6390x_ops too.

Fixes: f39908d3b1c4 ("net: dsa: mv88e6xxx: Set the CMODE for mv88e6390 ports 9 & 10")
Signed-off-by: Martin Hundebøll <mnhu@prevas.dk>
Reviewed-by: Andrew Lunn <andrew@lunn.ch>
Reviewed-by: Vivien Didelot <vivien.didelot@savoirfairelinux.com>
Signed-off-by: David S. Miller <davem@davemloft.net>

diff --git a/drivers/net/dsa/mv88e6xxx/chip.c b/drivers/net/dsa/mv88e6xxx/chip.c
index 53b088166c28..5bcdd33101b0 100644
--- a/drivers/net/dsa/mv88e6xxx/chip.c
+++ b/drivers/net/dsa/mv88e6xxx/chip.c
@@ -3178,6 +3178,7 @@ static const struct mv88e6xxx_ops mv88e6390x_ops = {
 	.port_set_jumbo_size = mv88e6165_port_set_jumbo_size,
 	.port_egress_rate_limiting = mv88e6097_port_egress_rate_limiting,
 	.port_pause_limit = mv88e6390_port_pause_limit,
+	.port_set_cmode = mv88e6390x_port_set_cmode,
 	.port_disable_learn_limit = mv88e6xxx_port_disable_learn_limit,
 	.port_disable_pri_override = mv88e6xxx_port_disable_pri_override,
 	.stats_snapshot = mv88e6390_g1_stats_snapshot,
-- 
2.25.1

### Modifications in Each File

1. **File: `drivers/net/dsa/mv88e6xxx/chip.c`**
   - Added the line `	.port_set_cmode = mv88e6390x_port_set_cmode,` to the `mv88e6390x_ops` structure. This change enables the configuration of the CMODE for the 6390X family of devices.

### Relationships Between Modifications

The modification in `chip.c` directly addresses a previously identified limitation in the support for the CMODE configuration for the 6390X family of devices. By adding the `port_set_cmode` function pointer to the `mv88e6390x_ops`, the patch ensures that the CMODE can now be set for the 6390X, thereby fixing the oversight mentioned in the earlier commit (f39908d3b1c4). This change enhances the functionality of the driver by providing complete support for CMODE configuration across the relevant device family.

net: dsa: mv88e6xxx: Enable CMODE config support for 6390X
MIME-Version: 1.0

Commit f39908d3b1c45 ('net: dsa: mv88e6xxx: Set the CMODE for mv88e6390
ports 9 & 10') added support for setting the CMODE for the 6390X family,
but only enabled it for 9290 and 6390 - and left out 6390X.

Fix support for setting the CMODE on 6390X also by assigning

Fixes: f39908d3b1c4 ("net: dsa: mv88e6xxx: Set the CMODE for mv88e6390 ports 9 & 10")
Signed-off-by: Martin Hundebøll <mnhu@prevas.dk>
Reviewed-by: Andrew Lunn <andrew@lunn.ch>
Reviewed-by: Vivien Didelot <vivien.didelot@savoirfairelinux.com>
Signed-off-by: David S. Miller <davem@davemloft.net>

Here is the root cause:
The root cause of the bug was the oversight in the driver code where support for setting the CMODE was not implemented for the 6390X family of devices, even though it was added for similar devices in a prior commit. This resulted in the lack of functionality to configure the CMODE on 6390X ports, leading to incomplete driver support for these devices.

The code statements that lead to the bug are:
```c
.port_set_cmode = NULL,
```
Reason:
The `.port_set_cmode` function pointer was not assigned for the 6390X family, resulting in the inability to set the CMODE for these devices, which was an oversight after similar functionality was added for other device families.

The code statements that fix the bug are:
```c
.port_set_cmode = mv88e6390x_port_set_cmode,
```
Reason:
By assigning the `mv88e6390x_port_set_cmode()` function to the `.port_set_cmode` function pointer, the patch enables the configuration of CMODE for the 6390X family, thus providing complete driver support for these devices.
